payload.rationale: I assign a 25% chance as a background-based judgment, not a September 2026 observational nowcast. The event requires NASA GISS’s reported unsmoothed annual Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2026 to exceed both 1.28°C and its 2025 value; matching either threshold is insufficient. Continued human-caused warming makes another record plausible, but 1.28°C is a demanding threshold, associated with the exceptional warmth of 2024. Annual variability, including ENSO and its delayed temperature effects, means warming does not produce a new record every year. Without supplied 2026 measurements or the reported 2025 value, I place the probability below one-half while allowing a substantial chance of exceedance. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that cooler ocean conditions or an unusually high 2025 comparator could make the required annual value unlikely. The strongest reason it could be too low is that persistent ocean warmth, faster recent warming, or favorable ENSO conditions could already have put 2026 on a record-setting trajectory. Those possibilities are uncertainties, not observations supplied here.
limitations: No outside evidence records were supplied, and no browsing or tools are available.
The 2025 NASA GISS annual value and 2026 monthly observations are not established by the supplied information.
This estimate cannot incorporate the substantial year-to-date evidence ordinarily available by September 19, 2026.
Resolution depends on the contract-defined NASA GISS series and reported precision; strict exceedance, rounding, and applicable data revisions can matter near the thresholds.
